Conflicting opinions and research outcomes — Sources differ on whether supplements are universally necessary or only needed when diet or fortified foods are insufficient.

Not all vegans necessarily need dietary supplements, because some sources say vegans can meet needs through fortified foods instead of pills, especially for vitamin B12 [d3][d6]. However, several sources say an unsupplemented vegan diet risks deficiencies and emphasize reliable B12 intake from supplements or fortified foods, with other supplements needed in some cases such as vitamin D or calcium [d4][d5][d1]. So the retrieved evidence supports a conditional answer: supplements are not universally required for every vegan, but some reliable non-plant source of key nutrients—especially B12—is required, and supplements are often recommended or needed [d3][d4][d6].
